title: Air Florida 90
summary: Boeing 737 crashed into the 14th Street Bridge over the Potomac River after takeoff from Washington National Airport on a snowy day. The pilots failed to activate engine anti-ice systems despite heavy snow and below-freezing temperatures, resulting in iced engine inlet sensors. This produced false low engine pressure ratio readings of 1.70 instead of the required 2.04 for takeoff. The aircraft departed with insufficient power and struck the bridge, destroying 97 feet of guard rail before plunging into the icy river. The investigation determined the pilots lacked experience in snowy conditions and failed to follow critical pre-flight procedures.
probable_cause: The pilots failed to activate engine anti-ice systems in freezing conditions with heavy snow, which allowed ice to accumulate on engine inlet probes. False EPR readings indicated insufficient thrust was set, but the pilots nonetheless proceeded with takeoff. The crew's lack of experience flying in snowy weather and failure to follow proper procedures led to insufficient power for flight and crash into the Potomac River.

title: 1982 Thunderbirds Indian Springs Diamond Crash
summary: Four U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds T-38A Talon jets crashed at Indian Springs Air Force Auxiliary Field, Nevada, during formation flying practice of a line abreast loop maneuver. The lead aircraft had a jammed stabilizer that prevented normal pitch control during descent at more than 400 mph. The other three pilots maintained formation in accordance with their training and did not break away, resulting in all four aircraft striking the desert floor almost simultaneously at high speed.
probable_cause: Jammed stabilizer on the lead aircraft prevented recovery during descent. Formation flying procedures and training prevented the wingmen from breaking away when the lead aircraft became uncontrollable.

title: World Airways 30
summary: World Airways Flight 30 touched down 2800 feet beyond the displaced threshold at Boston Logan on a runway covered with ice. Despite poor braking conditions reported as fair to poor, the aircraft could not be stopped on the runway. The pilots steered the aircraft off the runway to avoid obstacles and it skidded across a field and taxiway before coming to rest in Boston Harbor. The cockpit section submerged but 210 occupants survived. Two passengers, father and son, were missing and presumed drowned. A Delta flight had warned of nil braking conditions 35 minutes prior but this was not relayed to Flight 30.

title: Japan Air Lines 350
summary: Japan Air Lines Flight 350, a Douglas DC-8 on final approach to Tokyo, crashed into Tokyo Bay on 9 February 1982, killing 24 of the 174 occupants. The investigation determined the crash resulted from deliberate actions by Captain Katagiri, who disengaged the autopilot and pushed the aircraft into descent at 164 feet altitude despite efforts by the first officer and flight engineer to regain control. Investigators attributed the incident to auditory hallucinations experienced by Katagiri and the absence of proper medical examinations despite his known psychiatric condition.

summary: De Havilland DHC-6 Twin Otter Flight 933 crashed into the Barents Sea on 11 March 1982 near Gamvik, Norway, killing all 15 people on board. The aircraft was a scheduled service from Kirkenes to Alta with intermediate stops. The pilot chose visual flight rules in clear conditions but encountered strong turbulence between 1000 and 1500 feet. Investigation found cracks in the torque tube connecting the port elevator to the control system. The direct cause was structural failure of the vertical stabilizer following loss of elevator control.

title: Aeroflot 411
summary: The Il-62M took off from Sheremetyevo at 12:33 with 80 passengers and 10 crew. Within seconds, engine fire warnings were annunciated for engines one and two. title: Pan Am 759
summary: Pan Am Flight 759 crashed in Kenner, Louisiana, minutes after takeoff when the Boeing 727 encountered a microburst that produced a downdraft and decreasing headwind. The aircraft lifted off and climbed briefly then began to descend, striking trees. Eight people on the ground were killed. The NTSB determined the probable cause was microburst-induced wind shear during liftoff.
probable_cause: The aircraft's encounter with microburst-induced wind shear during liftoff, which imposed a downdraft and a decreasing headwind. Contributing factors included the limited capability of then-current wind shear detection technology.

summary: A US Army CH-47C Chinook transport helicopter carrying parachutists on a rehearsal jump took off from Mannheim City Airport. The aircraft struck airport structures, a highway, vehicles, and buildings before bursting into flames.
